name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite. Levers vs baseline (endogenous-rule era): AI cognitive labor payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5), robot integration friction halved (robotIntegrationExponent 0.5, diffusion 0.30), datacenter power-spend ceiling 10x (0.5% of GDP). FINDING (round-2, reconfirmed under the endogenous rules): the binding constraint is NOT the capex budget — the savings pool funds even ~$200T/yr of robot capex (unfundedRealizedSpend stays 0) — but the COST OF CAPITAL: WACC rises to ~15% by 2075 as automation, energy buildout, and CDR compete for savings, raising LCOE and entering the robot business case directly through the deployment rule's interest-rate term. Result (2026 model): GDP 2100 ~$3,300T, generation ~3.5M TWh, robots ~55,000/1000 workers, datacenters ~630k TWh riding their spend ceiling, warming ~2.8C. Sustained real rates >12% and densities of ~55 robots/person are outside anything observed — read as a financing-limited upper-envelope hypothesis, not a forecast.
